A1.justification: Both 36-page PDFs describe the same ConFIG research and include Appendices A.1–A.13. Text comparison, full-page rendering comparison, and inspection of the differing pages support reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original PINN training and CelebA multi-task experiments in Section 4, with numerical results, runtime measurements, additional PDE experiments, and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original PINN and CelebA experiments, including numerical results and supplementary analyses in Appendices A.5–A.13.

M1.justification: The ConFIG gradient construction, magnitude adjustment, and M-ConFIG momentum procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendix algorithms. The wording edit in Section 4.2 does not introduce a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four main PINN cases, the PNd, HeatMS, and KS problems in Appendix A.11, and the same CelebA task configurations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. The PINN comparisons retain their existing baselines, and CelebA Tables 14–15 retain the same ten comparison methods.

E3.justification: Metrics, training budgets, sampling, model configurations, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Section 4.2 replaces 'iterations' with 'gradient update', but the explicit updates-per-iteration setting and the experiments in Tables 18–19 already appear in v2.

E4.justification: Direction-weight tests, momentum-strategy comparisons, task/update-count analyses, challenging-PDE failure analyses, and learning-rate/sample-count ablations are retained unchanged in Figure 8, Figure 12, and Appendices A.5, A.11, and A.13.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging three training runs initialized with different random seeds and retain the same standard-deviation reporting in the appendix tables. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 15 retains best CelebA F1 scores of 0.694 ± 0.005 for M-ConFIG 30 and 0.686 ± 0.006 for ConFIG; the edited captions do not alter table entries.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, convergence theorems and proofs, comparator derivations, and solution-existence and equivalence arguments in Appendices A.1–A.4 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about conflict-free updates, balanced projections, adaptive magnitudes, momentum acceleration, and performance on PINNs and multi-task learning.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations concerning momentum-update frequency, memory, and difficult PDEs remain unchanged. The Section 4.2 wording correction restates the updates-per-iteration interpretation already explicitly explained in v2.

D1.justification: Implementation guidance, hyperparameters, sampling instructions, hardware, training times, and sample counts in Appendices A.5 and A.12 and Table 23 are unchanged. Code-access statements and external link targets also remain identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning against PCGrad and IMTL-G in Section 3.2, and the bibliography are unchanged. No cited work or substantive research positioning is added or removed.

P1.justification: Limited edits standardize ConFIG capitalization, including the Appendix A.5 heading and several captions, and replace 'number of iterations' with 'number of gradient update' in Section 4.2. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 12 and Tables 16–19 receive caption edits and local line rewrapping. Table 18 introduces the stray text 'METof'; plots, table structures, axes, legends, and figure/table placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves naming consistency and clarifies a sentence whose updates-per-iteration meaning was already explicit in v2. These small editorial gains accompany a new 'METof' typo in Table 18. With methods, evidence, theory, and reproducibility information unchanged, the edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.
